claims.statement: Joe Coburn sparred with Tom Allen at the Bowery Theater, New York, when Allen first came to America.
claims.excerpt:
I sparred
with him ia the Bowery Theater, New
York

claims.statement: Coburn knocked Tom Allen off the stage at the Bowery Theater, slightly injuring him.
claims.excerpt:
E-knocked
him off the stage, by which he
was slightly injured.

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Joe Coburn sparred at a benefit for Mike Coburn at Harry Hill's in New York, about seven or eight months before April 1876.
claims.excerpt:
did spar with hit at a
benefit given my brether, Mike Cobera,
at Harry Hills

claims.statement: Tom Allen would spar with Joe Coburn only on condition that Coburn promise not to throw him, and Coburn gave that promise.
claims.excerpt:
he would spar with me_ provided
I gave him a promise that I would not

claims.statement: Joe Coburn says Jem Mace beat Tom Allen in eleven and one-half minutes.
claims.excerpt:
Jem Mace fought and badly
beat Alen in
ELEVEN AND ONE-HALF MINUTES

claims.statement: The Adelphi manager says Tom Allen has sent his wife out of St. Louis and converted his property into cash, so that he can leave at any time.
claims.excerpt:
has sent his wife
out of the city, and converted all his property into cash

claims.statement: The Adelphi manager had not seen Tom Allen since March 18, 1876.
claims.excerpt: that fighter since the 18th of last month

fights.notes: Coburn's account, one side only; no date given. Probably the 1870 bout described in article 281, which says about ten rounds.

notes: Coburn's statement, one side; the Adelphi manager's replies are also included. Coburn's own career details are skipped. The 1868 and 1875 sparring dates are approximate from 'about eight years ago' and 'seven or eight months ago'.
